common_name: Scaly-Foot Hydrothermal Vent Gastropod (Greigite Iron-Sulfide Armor)

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Chrysomallon squamiferum (2.0 nm, detail scale)

paleobiology.chronoseries_note: The only node is the living species at 0 Ma. There is no successor chronospecies.
paleobiology.predecessor_comparison: Sclerite-less peltospirid Gigantopelta (Chen et al. 2015, 10.1111/zoj.12279) lacks the iron-sulfide foot sclerites. The 20 nm nanocrystal-packing wavelength is a coarser phenomenon size, not this slot's parameter set. At 2.0 nm the extant animal's detail mode is tenfold shorter, about two greigite unit cells.

equations.kinetics: du/dt = a - u + u^2 v + D_u lap u; dv/dt = b - u^2 v + D_v lap v
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)
equations.boundary_conditions: periodic on a rectangular nm-scale domain (spectral IMEX)

parameters.note: Chosen for this 2.0 nm detail slot. Not copied from the 20 nm sibling.

empirical_claims.claim: Dermal sclerites of the hot-vent gastropod are mineralized with iron sulfides including greigite and pyrite.
The scaly-foot shell and sclerites form a multilayer iron-sulfide armor whose mechanical performance was measured at the microscale. The paper does not state a Turing equation.
Chrysomallon squamiferum is the scaly-foot gastropod (Peltospiridae).
Scale and shell biomineralization deploy different subsets of an ancient lophotrochozoan toolkit.
Relative to sclerite-less Gigantopelta aegis, Chrysomallon co-opted biomineralization proteins into the scleritome.
A diffusion-driven instability selects wavenumber k_c. This slot sets lambda_c = 2.0 nm by solving for the diffusivities. That wavelength is not a measurement reported by the armor papers.

transfer_boundary: No source measures a 2.0 nm pigment stripe on this snail. The length is the slot's detail-scale critical wavelength, about two greigite unit cells (a ≈ 0.988 nm).
Aqueous Turing wavelengths are much longer. The 2 nm mode assumes matrix-confined diffusivities.
